title: Pluggable methodologies
description:
## Objective

As a team adopting Kanbus, I want the software-process opinions Kanbus teaches agents to come from pluggable **methodologies** I pick and combine, so that Kanbus is a neutral instrument of record and does not bring one hard-coded process with it.

Today `CONTRIBUTING_AGENT.md` is rendered from a single built-in template that hard-codes outside-in Behavior-Driven Design (The Cognitive Framework, Roles in the Order, The Rite of Gherkin, The Outside-In Ritual, Coverage) next to neutral Kanbus mechanics (hierarchy, workflows, priorities, commands, wiki, console). The agents file context also hard-codes a Gherkin example and a `has_story` flag.

## Shape

A methodology is a skill-like bundle: a directory with a `METHODOLOGY.md` (frontmatter plus Markdown body, rendered with the same template context) and optional `tools/` with scripts or commands the methodology teaches agents to use. It is like an agent skill, but its content is assembled into the generated `CONTRIBUTING_AGENT.md` rather than loaded on demand.

```yaml
methodologies:
  - bdd                       # built in
  - git-flow                  # built in
  - path: methodologies/crap  # project-provided bundle with tools
```

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  C[.kanbus.yml methodologies] --> R[Resolve built-in names and local paths]
  R --> M[Render each METHODOLOGY.md]
  K[Core Kanbus mechanics template] --> A[Assemble]
  M --> A
  A --> F[CONTRIBUTING_AGENT.md]
```

## Rules

- When `methodologies` is absent, the default is `[bdd, git-flow]`, built into the binary, with no files needed in the repository. Today's generated output stays equivalent for existing installations.
- `methodologies: []` yields a core-only agents file with no process opinions.
- More than one methodology can be active; they render in the configured order.
- No Gherkin- or BDD-specific behavior is hard-coded in core Kanbus. "Stories contain Gherkin" becomes a convention of the BDD methodology, not a rule of Kanbus. Gherkin as the language of Kanbus policy-as-code, and generic syntax validation of fenced `gherkin` blocks, are Kanbus features and stay.
- Rust and Python implementations stay in parity.
- `router.workflow` and existing configuration keys are untouched.

## Milestones

1. Built-in BDD and Git Flow methodologies assembled into the agents file.
2. Project-provided methodology bundles.
3. Methodology tools, proven with a CRAP complexity-reduction methodology.
4. Methodology commands, doctor checks and documentation.

## Definition of done

Behavior specifications for selection, defaults, ordering, custom bundles and tools pass in both implementations; this repository regenerates its own `CONTRIBUTING_AGENT.md` from methodologies; the authoring guide lets someone write a new methodology without reading Kanbus source.
